title: Callbacks, events, and debounce/throttle interview drills

items.question: Implement debounce and explain when to use it vs throttle.
items.answer: Debounce: clearTimeout on each call, schedule fn after wait ms with latest args. Use for search-as-you-type — wait until typing stops. Throttle: at most once per window — leading or trailing. Use for scroll/resize. Debounce on continuous scroll never fires until scroll stops.
items.sixtySeconds: Debounce quiet period. Throttle max rate. clearTimeout each call. cancel on unmount. AbortController with debounced fetch.

items.question: Why does debounced search need AbortController in addition to debounce?
items.answer: Debounce delays invocation but a slow fetch from an earlier keystroke can still resolve after a newer search started. Abort previous fetch when input changes. Catch AbortError. Debounce reduces calls; abort prevents stale results race.
items.sixtySeconds: Debounce limits frequency. Abort kills stale in-flight fetch. race without abort leaves zombie request.

items.question: What is event delegation and why use it on a long list?
items.answer: Attach one listener on parent container. On click, check event.target matches child selector. Fewer listeners, works for dynamically added rows, less memory. Bubbling phase delivers event from target up to parent.
items.sixtySeconds: One parent listener. target matches selector. Dynamic children work. Bubble phase default.

items.question: How do JavaScript events compare to C# delegates and events?
items.answer: JS: functions as callbacks, addEventListener/removeEventListener, no compile-time delegate types. C#: typed Delegate, event keyword with += -=, multicast. Both observer pattern. JS this binding matters on DOM handlers; C# sender parameter convention.
items.sixtySeconds: JS function callbacks. C# typed delegates. Both pub/sub. Remove listeners both languages.

items.question: A scroll handler runs 200 times per second and janks the UI. Fix it.
items.answer: Throttle to 100ms or requestAnimationFrame — not debounce. Throttle guarantees periodic updates during scroll. Use passive listener if not preventDefault. Avoid heavy layout reads in handler. Consider CSS transform instead of top/left.
items.sixtySeconds: Throttle scroll not debounce. rAF sync paint. passive true if no preventDefault.

items.question: Implement throttle with leading and trailing edge.
items.answer: Track lastCall timestamp. If window expired, invoke immediately (leading). Else schedule trailing setTimeout for remaining window if not already scheduled. clearTimeout on leading fire. Preserves last args in closure.
items.sixtySeconds: Timestamp window. Leading immediate if expired. Trailing setTimeout for mid-window calls. fn.apply for this.
